body:
On the CSV/default batch-Plan path the driver cannot register a bundle set, so the
session-end contract check asks only "did at least one `/handoff` pass?" and never
re-reads any brief:

```python
    if state.get("passed"):
        return []
```
— `template/src/pdca_harness/handoff.py` (`stop_problems`, the no-registered-bundles tail)

So a session that runs `/handoff issue_7` and then writes `issue_8/brief.md` with an
empty **Success criterion** ends with nothing reported. The id-seeded path
(`pdca flow <ids>`) is unaffected: those bundles are registered and each one's brief is
re-read.

## Why the gap matters: nothing else on that path catches it

Of the things the check would find, the CSV path leaves exactly one uncovered:

| Malformed brief | Caught later? |
|---|---|
| Unfilled template copy | Yes — `state.py` reads a placeholder brief as UNPLANNED |
| Dependency token with no `[[doctor.checks]]` row | Yes — `plan_policy` blocks before Do (`driver.py`, #333) |
| **Empty `Slug` / `Success criterion` / `Repo + branch target`** | **No** — `plan_policy` checks size and dependencies only |

An empty Success criterion therefore reaches Do, which has no stated end result to build
against, and then Check, which assembles SUMMARY §1 from the empty field
(`assemble.py`, `brief.whole_field`) and verifies the work against nothing. An empty
`Repo + branch target` leaves Do to guess the branch. This is the "the brief reads well
and demonstrates nothing" failure the exit contract exists to prevent.

## Shape of the fix

The data already exists one frame up: `do_plan_batch` snapshots every briefed bundle by
content hash *before* the session (`leaves.py`, the `briefed_before` map feeding the #301
plan-advisory pass). The contract check needs the same snapshot and can take it itself,
so no caller changes:

- In `handoff.session`, when the role is `planner` and no bundles were registered,
  record which `issue_*` dirs carry a `brief.md` and a hash of each — the same way the
  `act` role already captures its act-log baseline at session start.
- At the reap, run `check_planner` over every brief that is new or changed since that
  snapshot, and report the problems as usual (bundle-prefixed, report-only).
- A passing `/handoff` stays what it is — the session naming its work — but it no longer
  substitutes for re-reading the artifacts.

This is `handoff.py` only; `do_plan_batch` and the `/handoff` command are untouched.

## Notes

- Pre-existing: the retired #331 Stop hook used the same `stop_problems`, so the gap is
  not introduced by #534. What #534 changes is that the docs now describe this check as
  the thing that stops a session closing silently with a bad artifact, so the promise and
  the code should be brought together.
- Ordering: same file as #534, so this lands after it.
- Found during the #534 re-plan (round-4 adversarial review, item 1).
title: Batch Plan from a CSV: the session-end check never re-reads the briefs, so an empty Success criterion is reported by nothing
